_comment: Augmentum Marketplace catalog. Edit this file to add/remove curated
listings. Each listing names an `install_via` Source (js13k,
agsp-profile, internal, service_manifest, ...) and an
`install_payload` dict forwarded to that installer.
Entry naming: 'mkt:<short-slug>' for ids. Keep titles short. Use
the description for a paragraph; the tagline is the one-liner.
The catalog loader runs upsert-by-id and soft-delists removed
entries -- no migration needed.
kind='service' entries are SERVICE APP MANIFESTS (2026-07-18
service-OS design, docs/superpowers/specs/). Rules enforced at
load: install_via must be 'service_manifest'; image must be
version- or digest-pinned (':latest' rejected); the `browser`
block is REQUIRED (what does the user see after install?).
The prior game entries were removed 2026-06-17 (delist baseline).

listings.title: Uptime Kuma
listings.tagline: Self-hosted uptime monitoring with a beautiful status page.
listings.description: Monitor your services, websites, and APIs with notifications when something goes down. First launch opens a setup page to create your admin account. Runs entirely on your box.

listings.title: Navidrome
listings.tagline: Your music collection, streamed anywhere.
listings.description: A modern, fast music server and streamer for your own files. Point it at your music folder during install; the web player opens right after. Subsonic-compatible apps work out of the box.

listings.title: Radicale (Calendar & Contacts)
listings.tagline: A tiny CalDAV/CardDAV server for your calendars and contacts.
listings.description: Sync calendars and contacts across your devices without a cloud account. Works with iOS, Android (DAVx5), Thunderbird, and anything speaking CalDAV/CardDAV.

listings.title: Syncthing
listings.tagline: Continuous file sync between your devices, no cloud in between.
listings.description: Keeps folders in sync across your computers and phones, peer to peer and encrypted. First launch opens the web UI where you set a GUI password and add devices. Direct transfers use port 22000 when reachable; otherwise Syncthing falls back to community relays, which is slower but works everywhere.

listings.title: Vaultwarden
listings.tagline: Your own Bitwarden-compatible password vault.
listings.description: A lightweight server for the official Bitwarden apps and browser extensions. Everything is end-to-end encrypted with your master password. After install, create your account on the web vault, then point your Bitwarden clients at this server's HTTPS address.

listings.title: Stirling PDF
listings.tagline: Merge, split, rotate, convert, and edit PDFs in your browser.
listings.description: A complete PDF toolbox that runs entirely on your box — nothing you upload leaves it. Includes OCR in many languages, compression, page reordering, conversions, and more. Opens ready to use, no account needed.

listings.title: Memos
listings.tagline: Capture quick thoughts in a lightweight, private notes stream.
listings.description: A privacy-first note-taking service with markdown, tags, and a timeline view. The first account you create becomes the admin.

listings.title: flatnotes
listings.tagline: Database-less markdown notes — every note is a plain file.
listings.description: A clean note-taking app where each note lives as a Markdown file you can back up, sync, or edit with anything. You choose the admin password during install; sign in as 'admin'.

listings.title: Trilium Notes
listings.tagline: A personal knowledge base with an infinitely deep note tree.
listings.description: Build a structured knowledge base: hierarchical notes, cloning, relations, scripting, and encryption for protected notes. First launch walks you through setup and password creation.

listings.title: Pingvin Share
listings.tagline: Share files with anyone via links — a self-hosted WeTransfer.
listings.description: Upload files and get shareable links with optional expiry and passwords. The first account you register becomes the admin. Sharing outside your network requires this server to be reachable from outside.

listings.title: Duplicati
listings.tagline: Encrypted backups to any storage you already have.
listings.description: Back up to S3, Backblaze, Google Drive, OneDrive, SFTP, WebDAV, and more — always encrypted before it leaves your box. You set the web console password during install. Optionally point it at a library folder to include in backups.

listings.title: Mealie
listings.tagline: Recipe manager and meal planner — import recipes from any URL.
listings.description: Paste a recipe link and Mealie imports the ingredients and steps. Plan meals, build shopping lists, and share with your household. Create your account on first launch.

listings.title: Grocy
listings.tagline: Groceries, chores, and household management — beyond your fridge.
listings.description: Track what's in stock, what's expiring, chores, and shopping lists. Sign in with the default account (admin / admin) and change the password right away.

listings.title: HomeBox
listings.tagline: Inventory for your home — know what you own and where it is.
listings.description: Catalog your belongings with labels, locations, warranty details, and attachments. Register your account on first launch.

listings.title: Heimdall
listings.tagline: One tidy start page for all your self-hosted services.
listings.description: A simple, good-looking dashboard of links to everything you run. Opens ready to use — add your apps and links straight away.

listings.title: Wallos
listings.tagline: Track recurring subscriptions and see what they really cost.
listings.description: Log your subscriptions, get renewal reminders, and see monthly and yearly totals by category. Register your account on first launch.

listings.title: Calibre-Web
listings.tagline: A clean web library for browsing and reading your eBooks.
listings.description: Browse, read, and download your Calibre eBook library from any browser. Sign in with the default account (admin / admin123), change the password, then point it at your books folder.

listings.title: MeTube
listings.tagline: Download videos from YouTube and hundreds of other sites.
listings.description: A friendly web UI for yt-dlp: paste a link, pick a format, and the download lands in its library folder. Opens ready to use.

listings.title: Pinchflat
listings.tagline: Automatically archive YouTube channels and playlists.
listings.description: Subscribe to channels or playlists and Pinchflat keeps local copies as new videos land — built on yt-dlp, designed for media-server layouts. Opens ready to use; you can add a password in its settings.

listings.title: FreshRSS
listings.tagline: Follow every site you care about from one fast RSS reader.
listings.description: A free, self-hosted feed aggregator with keyboard-friendly reading, filters, and mobile client support. First launch runs a short setup wizard.

listings.title: LibreSpeed
listings.tagline: Test connection speed between your devices and this server.
listings.description: A lightweight, no-tracking speed test served from your own box — useful for checking your LAN and Wi-Fi, not just your internet. Opens ready to use.

listings.title: MySpeed
listings.tagline: Automatic speed tests with 30 days of history.
listings.description: Runs scheduled internet speed tests and charts the results so you can spot slowdowns and hold your ISP to its promises. Opens ready to use; a password can be set in its settings.

listings.title: changedetection.io
listings.tagline: Watch any web page and get notified when it changes.
listings.description: Track prices, restocks, job posts, or any page content, with flexible filters and dozens of notification targets. Opens ready to use; a password can be set in its settings.

listings.title: n8n
listings.tagline: Build automation workflows connecting hundreds of services.
listings.description: A visual workflow builder: triggers, branches, code steps, and integrations for hundreds of apps and APIs. Create the owner account on first launch.

listings.title: Node-RED
listings.tagline: Wire together devices, APIs, and services with visual flows.
listings.description: Low-code programming for event-driven automation — drag nodes, wire them up, deploy. Opens ready to use; admin auth can be enabled in its settings file.

listings.title: code-server
listings.tagline: VS Code in your browser, running on your own box.
listings.description: The full VS Code experience served from this machine — consistent dev environment from any device. You set the editor password during install.

listings.title: IT-Tools
listings.tagline: A big box of handy tools for developers, in one page.
listings.description:
⚙️ It-Tools is an open-source project hosted on GitHub that provides a collection of practical online tools for developers and IT professionals. The tools are designed to be easy to use, offering a great user experience. The project includes various features that simplify common tasks, such as URL decoding, QR code generation, JSON formatting, and XML formatting.

listings.title: Draw.io
listings.tagline: Diagramming and whiteboarding app.
listings.description: draw.io is a JavaScript, client-side editor for general diagramming and whiteboarding.

listings.title: CyberChef
listings.tagline: The Cyber Swiss Army Knife
listings.description: CyberChef is a web app for encryption, encoding, compression, and data analysis.

listings.title: Ntfy
listings.tagline: Ntfy, a simple server for sending and receiving notification messages.
listings.description: Send push notifications to any devices using a simple HTTP PUT or POST request. Note: installs open (no accounts) — add users and access control in its settings if this server is reachable beyond your LAN.

listings.title: Gotify
listings.tagline: Gotify, a simple server for sending and receiving notification messages.
listings.description: Simple server for sending and receiving notification messages.

listings.title: Beszel
listings.tagline: Lightweight server monitoring.
listings.description: A lightweight server monitoring hub with historical data, docker stats, and alerts.

listings.title: Actual Budget
listings.tagline: Local-first OpenSource Budget tool
listings.description: Actual is a local-first personal finance tool. It is 100% free and open-source, written in NodeJS, it has a synchronization element so that all your changes can move between devices without any heavy lifting.

listings.tagline: Kavita is a fast, feature rich, cross platform reading server
listings.description: Kavita is a fast, feature rich, cross platform reading server Point your library at the /media folder (optionally bound to a host folder at install).

listings.title: LibreTranslate
listings.tagline: Free and Open Source machine translation API
listings.description:
⚠️ Removal Notice: The LibreTranslate app has been disabled over trademark issues.

LibreTranslate is a free and Open Source Machine Translation API, entirely self-hosted. Unlike other APIs, it doesn't rely on proprietary providers such as Google or Azure to perform translations. listings.title: Open WebUI
listings.tagline: A familiar ChatGPT-style interface, wired to your Augmentum models automatically.
listings.description: A polished, self-hosted chat UI for large language models. On install, Augmentum points it at your own served models, voices, and transcription — no API keys to paste, no endpoints to configure. Sign in, pick a model, and chat. Your data stays in this container (SQLite); Augmentum handles HTTPS and access.

listings.tagline: Serve any Hugging Face model architecture the built-in engine cannot.
listings.description: A GPU inference engine (vLLM + llama-swap) for model architectures the bundled llama-server cannot load yet - brand-new archs served from their safetensors weights via trust_remote_code, hot-swapped by model name. Optional; installs with a one-time image download. Requires an NVIDIA GPU.

_comment: ADD-ONS (kind: 'addon', install_via: 'addon_build').
An add-on is not a service: it is a capability Augmentum gains,
not a product you open. No port, no healthcheck, no long-running
container -- the image is inventory the runtime spawns per session.
These entries carry PRESENTATION ONLY. Every buildable fact (image
tag, Dockerfile, pinned build args, dependencies, measured disk and
build time, license notice) lives in augmentum/addons/catalog.py and
is merged in by discover_routes, because a recipe and the code that
builds it must version together. The listing points at an addon_id.
listings.title: Console emulation
listings.tagline: Play GameCube, Wii and PS2 games, streamed to any device.
listings.description:
Adds console emulation to your Library. Augmentum builds Dolphin and PCSX2 on your machine, then streams them over WebRTC — so a game running on your tower is playable on a phone, tablet or TV with a controller, and picks up where you left off. Memory cards, save states and NAND persist per profile.

This is an add-on, not an app: nothing runs until you launch a title, and nothing appears in your browser tabs. Installing builds the image and keeps it available; uninstalling deletes the build and removes console emulation from Augmentum.

No games and no BIOS are included — you supply your own.

metadata.license: GPLv2 (Dolphin), GPLv3 (PCSX2) — built locally, not redistributed

listings.title: Luanti worlds
listings.tagline: A streamed voxel sandbox with persistent per-profile worlds.
listings.description:
Adds Luanti (the open-source voxel sandbox formerly called Minetest) to your Library as a streamed title. Worlds live on your server and survive container recycling, so you can build from a desktop and come back on a tablet.

This is an add-on, not an app: nothing runs until you launch a world. Installing builds the image and keeps it available; uninstalling deletes the build and removes Luanti from Augmentum. Your saved worlds are kept.

listings.title: Cast to TV
listings.tagline: Send Augmentum's own surfaces to a TV or receiver.
listings.description:
Adds casting of Augmentum's web surfaces — the 3D avatar, the notebook, the comic reader — to any receiver on your network. A headless browser renders the surface on your server and streams the result, so the receiving screen needs nothing but a browser.

This is an add-on, not an app: a renderer starts when you cast and stops when you're done. Installing builds the image and keeps it available; uninstalling deletes the build and removes casting of web surfaces from Augmentum.
